corpus.text: Lexical task classifier: keyword lists map task text to classes such as security, authentication, migration, release, deployment; classify returns the class, risk level, and mutation likelihood without calling any model.

Deterministic routing policy: fail-closed guards for missing or contradictory evidence, schema failures, and budget overruns; route picks deterministic tooling, Weavatrix analysis, bounded Ollama advice, or the upstream agent.

Deterministic context compiler: compile_context selects evidence items by priority under a token budget, reports included and omitted citation ids with saved-token estimates, and errors when critical evidence exceeds the budget.
Token estimation helper: estimate_tokens approximates token counts from character length for budget checks and savings accounting.
Native Weavatrix sessions per repository produce evidence fragments from graph_stats, module_map, context_bundle, and verified_change tool results with stable WX citation ids.

Fragment splitting: oversized tool results are packed into paragraph chunks under a character cap and emitted as ordered stable sub-citations like WX-VERIFY-1, so a budget keeps a prefix instead of dropping the fragment whole.
Weavatrix Refactor bridge is preview-only: the apply operation is never exposed, and confirmation or apply tokens are recursively stripped from requests and preview responses.
Evidence trust policy: symbol context is critical and can never be silently omitted, while plan-phase change plans stay unverified and force the requiresUpstream escalation flag.

Run engine: apply_command validates the expected revision, dispatches typed run commands, and appends exactly one durable event per command; create_run seeds node and edge states from the immutable graph snapshot.

Executor leases give one explicit identity exclusive execution of a run node: claim and release commands with bounded TTL, lazy expiry evaluated against command timestamps, and enforcement that rejects work from non-holders.
Run evidence: submissions are immutable and scoped to one node attempt; invalidation records an audited actor and reason and blocks future citations while preserving the original record.

Bounded retries: a retry controller node with a target and maxAttempts rewinds the forward closure of the failed node, reopening only that path; attempts are capped and the lease of the previous executor is cleared.
Deterministic replay: replay_events rebuilds a run from the created event, reapplies every recorded command with its recorded timestamp, and reports any mismatch instead of repairing state.
Human and review gates require an explicit approved or rejected decision with actor, reason, and same-attempt evidence references; generic completion commands are rejected on gate nodes.
Graph persistence: SQLite store with optimistic revisions where stale writes receive a conflict, and a history table that archives prior revisions of each graph.
Run persistence: runs are created from a graph snapshot and commands are applied transactionally, writing the updated document and the event in the same SQLite transaction.

Shadow mode observes route classification and context compression on a background worker thread with a bounded queue: overflow drops samples with a counter, and oversized compression payloads are skipped instead of producing timed-out samples.
Shadow sample store: append-only rows with SHA-256 input digests and no raw payloads; aggregates report schema validity, agreement rate, missed escalations, latency percentiles, and device breakdown.
Usage ledger: append-only records of every routing decision and context compilation with budget, raw, selected, and saved token counts, optionally attributed to a run id.
Quality-equivalent accounting: savings are credited only for runs that succeeded with no retried nodes and no rejected gates; everything else stays unproven.
Upstream self-reporting: executors report their own input and output token consumption per run to close the token balance without access to vendor billing.
Calibration runner: checks installed models without pulling, runs classification, extraction, and compression fixtures against a profile, aggregates metrics, and issues a role-aware verdict.

Pinned prompts and schemas shared by the benchmark and shadow mode: hard escalation rules for tier classification, verbatim field copying for extraction, and compression with an explicit Allowed IDs list.
Pure comparators: tier ranking with missed-escalation detection, bracketed citation scanning, hallucinated citation detection against supplied ids, and token estimate deltas.
Role-aware verdicts: a local_small profile is gated on classification and extraction, a local_medium profile on citation-preserving compression; off-role suites are reported but never gate.
Bounded loopback Ollama client: exact model tags only, structured chat with thinking disabled so JSON lands in content, budget validation, and no hidden model pulls or downgrades.
Local draft quality gate: structured drafts are parsed and rejected when the summary is empty, evidence ids are unknown, or unresolved issues remain; every failure falls back to the upstream agent.
The MCP server exposes bounded stdio tools: graph read and save, skill compile and export, route_work, weavatrix_context_compile, run controls, shadow metrics, and the usage ledger.
Vendor adapters render preview-only wiring for Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot from the canonical graph: skill instructions plus MCP registration files; the exporter never writes to disk.
Skill round trip: SKILL.md Markdown imports into typed workflow graphs with provenance, and canonical graphs export back to stable readable Markdown.
The HTTP server hosts the graph and run API plus the React SVG editor; run overlays render node and edge execution states directly on the canvas.
Single-file distribution: the built UI is embedded into the server binary with an SPA fallback route, while a directory flag still serves assets from disk during development.

Typed graph schema: node kinds including human gate, test gate, retry controller, local model, and upstream agent; edge kinds including sequence, success, failure, fallback, and approval; structural validation invariants.

queries.text: Where is the token budget enforced when selecting evidence for a context packet?
How do executor leases stop two agents from working on the same run node at once?
What guarantees that a run can be replayed deterministically and tampering is detected?
How are oversized Weavatrix results kept partially citable under a small budget?
Which component decides whether a task must go to the upstream coding agent?
How does shadow mode measure local models without slowing down real requests?
Where are token savings recorded and why are some savings not credited?
How is the refactor apply operation prevented from ever running?
What stops a local model draft with invented citation ids from being accepted?
How are human approval and rejection decisions recorded on a run?
How does a failed node get retried with a bounded number of attempts?
Which piece turns SKILL.md files into executable workflow graphs?
